questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial that the accepted that I only speak English and that some of the communication could happen in English. It was also crucial that I could feel somewhat safe at the destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It has been a great experience and I am so grateful for the opportunity provided by KU. The language barrier was greater that I anticipated which made the learning experience challenging (therefor 9/10).

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: To be honest, I found it very stressful to arrange everything for the exchange. I often felt like I had no clear overview of what was required or what I might be missing. However, when I reached out for help in Denmark, support was provided quickly, which was a relief. The greater challenge was with the receiving institution, where responses were not always timely.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had a meeting and a small introduction on the first day. While the arrival process was not the most organized—partly because I started earlier than most Erasmus students—I felt that I received the essential information I needed to get started.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The orientation week was held three weeks after I started, which is fair since I knew I was beginning earlier than most Erasmus students. However, I had a difficult start. The department I was initially assigned to was not very informative, and I was often left on my own. Not knowing the language or the workflow made it challenging to navigate. I wish the department had been better prepared for hosting Erasmus students, providing a proper introduction and more structured support.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I reached out to a former student from KU to ask where she had lived, and she kindly forwarded me the information, so I ended up staying in the same apartment. I felt very lucky with this arrangement, as I heard from other students that they faced a lot of trouble finding accommodation, and some even had issues with scams.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I highly recommend organizing your housing in advance and, if possible, try to secure accommodation in the city center. Be cautious of scammers—don't agree to pay extra rent to someone claiming to help you find accommodation. Many students found their housing through a Facebook group, and you'll receive a link to it in the introduction email from the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Because I found it by myself - I think that there could be more help from the university or ESN.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: II was a bit confused by the process, as the learning agreement had to be filled out before the application was due. However, it couldn't be signed by KU until I received the acceptance letter from UoC, which made the situation very unclear. The next student going to the same destination also encountered the same issue and reached out to me for help. I think this process should be better organized and clarified. Additionally, I spent a lot of time finding the right courses to fill out the learning agreement, as the UoC website was not very informative.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: KU signed the learning agreement before the acceptance letter.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Succesful - I got all the departments I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have trust that it will work out. Everybody also wants to help, but the response might be a bit delayed.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I was a bit disappointed with the academic level. As I mentioned earlier, the language barrier was a much bigger problem than I had anticipated. This made it very difficult to follow the workflow of the departments. Some departments did try to include me, but I found that it was a significant challenge for them to prioritize students given their heavy workload and busy schedules.

That said, I found that some departments were better than others, and I really enjoyed my time in the last department. It was the best clinical experience I have ever had. I learned so much there; they were exceptionally kind and inclusive.

While I have no doubt that the academic level is very high, it is challenging for a foreign student to gain meaningful learning experiences if they are not included in a language they can understand. I believe it is crucial for departments to be genuinely interested in hosting students. This commitment is essential to ensure that the academic goals of the stay are met.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: As I was on a clinical clerkship, I rotated through four different departments. In each department, I tried to integrate into their workflow by attending rounds, observing surgeries, participating in outpatient clinics, and engaging in other activities. The level of learning largely depended on how much I was included in these activities. Some departments provided more opportunities for hands-on learning and discussion, which greatly enhanced the experience, while others were more observational due to their workload and priorities.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
In the bigger picture, the style of teaching at my host institution had many similarities to that of UCPH. However, there were some notable differences. In clinical clerkships in Denmark, it is usually made very clear who the students are assigned to and what the schedule for the day looks like. At my host institution, this aspect was less structured, leaving it up to the student to figure out who to follow and what to focus on. This lack of clarity sometimes made it exhausting to navigate, especially as not everyone had the time or energy to accommodate an international student in their busy schedules.

Additionally, I would have appreciated more lectures. For example, having a weekly lecture for all Erasmus students, delivered by different departments, could have significantly increased the overall learning outcome and provided a more structured educational experience

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would highly recommend the neurosurgery department. It was the best department I attended during my clinical clerkship. The learning outcome from this department was outstanding, and the experience was truly exceptional.

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university had a library, a gym and a swimming pool. The ESN hosted so many great events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join all the ESN events

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: All the great beaches, all the great museums and also go for a trip to Athens (go by boat with student discount or flight). The other students visited Santorini by boat (student discount as well).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Adjusting to the local culture was very easy for the non-academic aspects. I absolutely loved the Greek culture and the warmth of the people, which made me feel welcome and comfortable. On the academic side, I had to adapt to a more flexible approach to scheduling and time management.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The Greek students are very easy to talk to and very including. I would recommend getting a buddy as well through ESN.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: As mentioned, the more flexible approach to scheduling and time management. That 8.00 might be 8.00 but it could also be 8.30 ish

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The warm and including culture of the local people. And the food.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Be Proactive and adaptable: unlike the structured system you might be used to, you will need to take the initiative to figure out your daily schedule and find someone to shadow in the departments. This might feel challenging at first, but it's an excellent opportunity to develop independence and adaptability.

2) Learn basic local language skills: the language barrier can be a challenge, so having some basic knowledge of Greek or being prepared to use translation tools can make a significant difference in your ability to follow the workflow.
3) Embrace the local culture: the warmth and hospitality of Greek culture are incredible, so take the time to enjoy it outside of academics. Engaging with the local lifestyle and building relationships will enrich your experience. 
AND participate in the ESN events - this is also where you find many of your new friends.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are a medical student attending the hospital, you should know that the canteen offers free lunch for students. I wasn't aware of this until three weeks into my stay, so make sure to take advantage of it right from the start!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was creating new international friendships and becoming part of a group of Erasmus students. Sharing the experience of exploring Greek culture together was truly amazing and made the exchange unforgettable.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge during the exchange was feeling unwelcome in certain departments and struggling with the language barrier. It was difficult to communicate effectively and to find opportunities to learn, often requiring extra effort to advocate for myself and be included.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
